summary.intent: Add branch as a real scope kind for memory loop records, plus scope filtering in the TUI (both browsing filter on Memories tab and injection scope toggles on Settings tab).
summary.outcome: Fully implemented: ScopeKindBranch added to data model, refresh now stores branch-scoped records, SelectRelevant gained functional options for scope filtering at injection time, Memories tab got an All/Repo/Me/Branch filter (S key) with cross-filtered counts, Settings tab got toggleable injection scope chips, and 5 new tests were added — all passing.

repo: Memory loop scope kinds live in cmd/entire/cli/memoryloop/memoryloop.go; Store struct holds InjectionScopes and the ScopeKind constants.
scopeKindForRefresh and resolveAddScope are in cmd/entire/cli/memory_loop_cmd.go and control how refresh maps CLI scope flags to stored record scopes.
Injection is triggered from lifecycle.go via maybeInjectMemoryLoop, which calls SelectRelevant — the right place to pass scope options.
The memorylooptui package has a dedicated tab_memories.go (browsing) and tab_settings.go (configuration) that are separate from the skill TUI in skilltui/.
Pre-existing lint failures exist in skilldb/discovery (ireturn issues from bubbletea pattern) and are not caused by new changes.
Pre-existing test failures exist in skilldb/discovery — unrelated to memory loop changes.
Local state files (.entire/insights.db, .entire/memory-loop.json, .superpowers/, HANDOFF_MEMORY_LOOP.md, memory-loop-architecture.html) should not be committed.

code.finding: InjectionScopes uses omitempty so existing JSON files without the field deserialize to nil, treated as 'all scopes' for backward compatibility — no migration needed.
scopeFilter and statusFilter are independent; statusCounts must be cross-filtered by scope (and vice versa) so chip counts always match visible table rows.
toggleScope prevents empty injection scopes — removing the last enabled scope is a no-op to avoid silently injecting nothing.
buildMemoryLoopSelectOpts helper resolves current git branch at injection time (distinct from refresh-time branch resolution in memory_loop_cmd.go) using the strategy package already imported.

workflow: Functional options pattern (SelectOption with WithInjectionScopes/WithCurrentBranch) is idiomatic Go for extending function signatures without breaking existing callers or tests.
Scope filtering should run before passesInjectionGate in the injection pipeline to avoid wasted tokenization and scoring on records that will be filtered out.
When staging a commit on a long-lived branch with pre-existing unstaged changes, stage only the files touched by the current feature rather than using git add -A.
Build verification (go build ./...) before writing tests catches compilation errors early and avoids test-time surprises.

friction: Initial confusion about whether memory loop scopes and the skill TUI's All/Repo/Personal filters were the same feature — they are completely separate systems.
Pre-existing lint errors (ireturn in bubbletea pattern) required manual verification that they weren't introduced by the new changes.
Pre-existing test failures in skilldb/discovery required isolation to confirm new tests were clean.
The working tree had many unrelated pre-existing modifications (skilldb, skilltui, permissions, insightsdb, root.go) that required careful selective staging for both commits.
open_items: The second commit ('commit everything') included skilldb, skilltui, permissions, insightsdb, and root.go changes that were pre-existing on the branch — their purpose and completeness is unknown and may need follow-up.
Pre-existing lint failures in skilldb/discovery (ireturn issues) were left unresolved.
Pre-existing test failures in skilldb/discovery were left unresolved.
HANDOFF_MEMORY_LOOP.md and memory-loop-architecture.html exist as untracked local files — unclear if they represent in-progress documentation that should eventually be committed or cleaned up.
